responsibility: Stage one of the pipeline. Fetch the SteamSpy bulk catalog, apply the coarse filter to isolate a candidate set, then fetch Steam appdetails and review summaries for the survivors only. Rate limit every request, retry safely, and persist all responses verbatim into raw_games.
design_notes: Two-stage funnel per ADR-004: bulk first, per-app second. Per-app calls are expected in the low thousands, not ~150k.
Official and documented endpoints only per ADR-003. No HTML parsing of Steam Store, SteamDB or SteamCharts.
Raw responses are written verbatim per ADR-005 so enrichment never needs the network.
Published rate limits for these endpoints are not authoritative. Defaults are conservative and live in config, not in code.

public_interface.name: RateLimiter
methods: def observe_response(self, status_code: int, headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> None
public_interface.description: Token bucket per host. observe_response honours Retry-After and widens the interval after 429 or 5xx. Raises RequestBudgetExceeded when the per-run budget is spent.

public_interface.name: HttpClient
methods: def get_json(self, url: str, params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> tuple[int, dict]
public_interface.description: Shared base: session reuse, timeout, custom User-Agent identifying the tool, exponential backoff with jitter, bounded retries. Returns (status_code, payload) rather than raising on 4xx so the status can be persisted.

public_interface.name: SteamSpyClient
methods: def fetch_all_page(self, page: int) -> tuple[int, dict]
def fetch_app(self, appid: int) -> tuple[int, dict]
public_interface.description: Wraps the SteamSpy API. The 'all' endpoint is paginated and heavily rate limited; page delay comes from AcquisitionConfig.

public_interface.name: SteamStoreClient
methods: def fetch_app_details(self, appid: int) -> tuple[int, dict]
public_interface.description: Wraps appdetails. Locale is fixed to cc=us&l=english as module-level constants, not caller-overridable (ARCHITECTURE.md locale-pinning decision, 2026-09-20) -- so price and review fields are comparable across every run, not just within one run.

public_interface.name: SteamReviewsClient
methods: def fetch_review_summary(self, appid: int) -> tuple[int, dict]
public_interface.description: Wraps the reviews endpoint requesting the summary only (zero review bodies) to keep payloads small.

public_interface.name: fetch_steamspy_catalog
public_interface.signature: def fetch_steamspy_catalog(client: SteamSpyClient, *, max_pages: int | None = None, on_event: EventSink) -> Iterator[RawPayload]
public_interface.description: Yields one RawPayload per app from the paginated bulk endpoint. Streams so the caller can persist in batches without holding the catalog in memory.

public_interface.name: build_catalog_frame
public_interface.description: Flattens bulk payloads into columns: appid, name, developer, publisher, positive, negative, owners_low, owners_high, price_usd, initialprice, discount, tags.

public_interface.name: coarse_filter
public_interface.signature: def coarse_filter(catalog: pd.DataFrame, criteria: CoarseFilterCriteria) -> FunnelResult
public_interface.description: Applies the stage-one band. Returns survivors plus a per-reason rejection tally so the funnel stays auditable.

public_interface.name: fetch_app_details
public_interface.signature: def fetch_app_details(client: SteamStoreClient, appids: Sequence[int], *, on_event: EventSink) -> Iterator[RawPayload]

public_interface.name: fetch_review_summaries
public_interface.signature: def fetch_review_summaries(client: SteamReviewsClient, appids: Sequence[int], *, on_event: EventSink) -> Iterator[RawPayload]

public_interface.name: run_acquisition
public_interface.signature: def run_acquisition(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, config: AcquisitionConfig, settings: Settings, *, on_event: EventSink) -> AcquisitionReport
public_interface.description: Stage entry point called by orchestration. Executes bulk fetch -> persist -> coarse filter -> per-app fetch -> persist, emitting progress events throughout.

public_interface.name: RequestBudgetExceeded
public_interface.description: Subclass of AcquisitionError. Fails the run loudly instead of continuing to hammer an API.

coarse_filter_contract.note: Threshold values are PROPOSED in FORMULATION.md section 7 and are supplied through CoarseFilterCriteria. The implementation must not embed any default band.

invariants: Every request passes through RateLimiter.acquire() first; no direct requests.get anywhere in the module
Response bodies are persisted exactly as received, including error bodies, with their HTTP status
A failed per-app fetch degrades that app, never the run: it is recorded and reported, and the run continues
Per-app fetches happen only for appids present in FunnelResult.candidates
Payloads are persisted in batches as they stream in, so a crash mid-stage leaves usable partial data
edge_cases: SteamSpy 'all' returns an empty page or repeats the previous page -> stop pagination, emit a warning event
appdetails returns {"<appid>": {"success": false}} -> persist verbatim with success=false, count as detail_failed, do not retry indefinitely
appdetails returns a non-game app_type (dlc, demo, video, music, tool) -> persist; exclusion happens in enrichment, not here
HTTP 429 with Retry-After -> sleep the stated interval, then resume; repeated 429 widens the base interval for the rest of the run
HTTP 5xx -> bounded exponential backoff with jitter, then mark the app failed
Connection reset / timeout / DNS failure -> same retry path as 5xx
Response is not valid JSON (HTML error page) -> persist the raw text with its status and mark failed; never attempt to parse it as a store page
Duplicate appid across bulk pages -> de-duplicated in build_catalog_frame, counted as duplicate_appid
Empty candidate set after coarse filter -> stage succeeds with candidate_count=0 and emits a warning; downstream stages must handle an empty run
Missing STEAM_WEB_API_KEY where required -> AcquisitionError before any request is issued
Clock/date parsing: release_date strings from Steam are locale-formatted and may be partial ('2019', 'Q3 2020', 'Coming soon') -> parse leniently, store the unparsed original

unit: RateLimiter spaces calls to the configured interval (monotonic clock injected, no real sleeping in tests)
RateLimiter honours Retry-After and raises RequestBudgetExceeded at the budget
HttpClient retries on 5xx and timeout, stops after max_retries, returns the final status
build_catalog_frame parses a recorded SteamSpy page fixture into the expected columns and dtypes
coarse_filter tallies each rejection reason correctly on a synthetic catalog covering every boundary
coarse_filter boundary behaviour is inclusive/exclusive exactly as specified at min and max review count
fetch_app_details records success=false payloads as failures without aborting the batch
non-JSON response is persisted and marked failed
integration: run_acquisition against a stubbed HTTP layer writes the expected raw_games rows, funnel report and event sequence for a 20-app synthetic catalog
testing.policy: No test may perform a real network call.

non_goals: No field normalization or derived features (that is enrichment)
No scraping of any HTML property
No incremental/delta fetch against a previous run in v1 (parent_run_id exists for this later)
open_questions: Country/currency pinning for appdetails: 'us' assumed. Confirm before locking, since it fixes the price basis of every revenue estimate.
Whether to also store steamspy_appdetails per candidate for tag votes, or to rely on the tag data already in the bulk payload.
